_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.

THE HANG THAT KILLED TWO SESSIONS IS ROOT-CAUSED, one defect with three symptoms: pty::spawn forks and the child calls unsetenv (pty.rs:211), which takes glibc's environment lock - held at fork time by a grants::tests thread inside set_var, so it can never be released in the child. The child deadlocks in __lll_lock_wait_private and NEVER REACHES execvp, so FD_CLOEXEC never fires and it holds every inherited fd forever: both read_sync pipe write-ends and another test's UnixStream::pair server end whose parent had already dropped it. Proven from /proc and eu-stack on two independent instances, one hung 4 h 03 m. Nothing there has a deadline. Now dispatched as suite-reliability.

A DEAD AGENT'S PROCESSES OUTLIVE ITS SESSION. A mutation battery from an agent that died at 22:45 was still running four hours later, blocked on the hung cargo, and RESUMED SPLICING MUTANTS INTO THE WORKTREE the moment the hang cleared. Check what is actually running before concluding a hang or a dirty file is yours - and the p2-010 successor's 'one dirty path to finish' turned out to be exactly that: a spliced mutant, restored rather than committed.

THE CI CGROUP QUESTION HAD A THIRD ANSWER. in-login-session.sh WORKS on a GitHub runner (logind session 2, session-2.scope, uid 1001); the two failures were in a deliberately unwrapped step asserting rules that are functions of the request alone while sitting behind an origin observation that fails there. Moved ahead of it: refuses strictly more, never less. Reproducible locally with no sudo via `unshare -C --map-current-user`, which yields cgroup 0::/ and matches neither branch of classify - 9/2 before, 11/0 after. That mechanism is reusable.

FLEET HAZARD, FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE IT WAS TRIGGERED. build-image.yml has had workflow_dispatch since 48fb1b26 - the brief that sent an agent to 'add workflow_dispatch' was working from a false premise - and its promote step was gated on the string test 'the push produced a digest' and nothing else, while push-retry.sh always moved the floating :core and :base tags. ONE DISPATCH FROM ANY REF WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THAT BRANCH TO EVERY DEPLOYED MACHINE and poisoned the next main build's core. The agent found it while acting on a brief that told it to dispatch a build, and fixed it BEFORE dispatching. Now gated on github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', proven by executing the extracted shell against stub podman and skopeo: a non-main ref writes 4 per-SHA tags and no floating name; main writes 17, byte-identical to the pre-patch set.

THE FORK/unsetenv DEADLINE CAUGHT THE RACE ON ITS FIRST RUN: a four-hour hang became a named failure in 10.01 s. The fix builds the environment and the full PATH candidate list in the PARENT and hands them to execve, because between fork and exec only async-signal-safe calls are legal. Mutant (child takes the env lock again): 5 of 5 runs wedged on spawn 1 or 2 of 300. Fixed: 300/300 clean, 5 runs of 5.

_ci: CI RAN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM, and this is the record of what that cost and bought. pr-validation.yml triggered ONLY on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and the program is forbidden from opening a PR until final integration - so sixty landed items, twelve landings and ~2000 Rust tests had been verified on exactly one laptop. `gh run list --branch roadmap/v2.2` returned nothing at all. Fixed in four commits, each one exposing the next problem: (1) push + workflow_dispatch triggers added; the first run failed in 18s. (2) The parity check cloned apex-shell's DEFAULT branch, so it compared apex-os roadmap/v2.2 against apex-shell main and reported drift on two touchpad defaults - while the two INTEGRATION branches agreed perfectly at 22 settings. It now clones the matching branch and PRINTS which one it used. THE DRIFT IT EXPOSED IS REAL AND IS KEPT: apex-shell main has drag_lock=true and click_method=clickfinger where apex-os main's generator has false and buttonAreas, so whoever does the final integration must land both sides together or opening the Input page silently changes a user's touchpad behaviour. (3) The path classifier read github.event.pull_request.* and died with exit 128 on a push; it is now event-aware and, when no range can be determined, selects EVERYTHING - this file already records four occasions where a selector picked nothing, the job skipped, and the workflow passed. (4) Six confinement assertions in mcp_sidecar_live.rs had never run anywhere but the L16 because the runner has no bubblewrap; installed rather than skipped, because they are the assertions that the sandbox IS a sandbox. Then bwrap failed on Ubuntu 24.04's kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, so the sysctl is relaxed and PROVEN with a smoke check before any test runs. THE FINDING THAT PAYS FOR ALL OF IT: on the runner, /proc/N/cgroup reads '/system.slice/hosted-compute-agent.service', which is neither a login session nor a user service - a THIRD classification distinct from the L16's session scope and from scheduled-job. Two request_origin tests fail there while nine pass. Four rounds of orchestrators wrote that the workflow file was the only evidence of what CI presents; it is now measured, and p0-014 has been sent the exact string while it is still live.
